In force-current analogy, mechanical force is analogous to electrical current, and velocity is analogous to voltage.  
A dash-pot in mechanical systems provides a damping force proportional to velocity: \( F = B v \), where \( B \) is the damping coefficient.  
In force-current analogy, force \( F \) maps to current \( i \), and velocity \( v \) maps to voltage \( V \).  
So \( i = B v \) becomes \( i = B V \), which is Ohm’s law \( i = G V \) where \( G \) is conductance.  
Thus, the dash-pot is analogous to electrical conductance.  

Final answer: (B)
